skill.name: open-show
skill.description: Convert Markdown, Word, PDF, text, local HTML, or URLs into a single full-screen HTML slideshow.
skill.summary: Creates portable HTML presentation decks from documents and web pages.
skill.author: lumacoder

security_audit.summary: No prompt-injection language was found in SKILL.md or README.md. Confirmed risks are arbitrary URL and image fetching, a TLS verification bypass fallback, DOCX media reads without size limits, and unsafe preservation of untrusted HTML in generated decks. Most other static alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, keyboard event code, CSS, and documented .hermes paths.

remediation.issue: TLS certificate verification can be disabled during URL fetch retry.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the verify=False fallback, or require explicit user confirmation with a clear warning before insecure fetching.

remediation.issue: Generated HTML can preserve untrusted markup and attributes.
remediation.suggestion: Escape text by default and sanitize HTML with an allowlist that removes scripts, event attributes, and javascript: URLs.

remediation.issue: URL and image fetching accepts arbitrary remote destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Block private, loopback, and link-local addresses, enforce response size limits, and keep strict timeouts.

remediation.issue: DOCX media is read from compressed archives without visible size limits.
remediation.suggestion: Limit total decompressed media bytes and reject overly large archive members before reading them into memory.

remediation.issue: External browser launch is available through command flags.
remediation.suggestion: Keep subprocess arguments fixed and require explicit user opt-in before using --open or --openclaw.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Markup Preserved in Generated HTML
semantic_findings.description: HTML and Markdown input blocks are stored as raw HTML and then inserted into the generated deck. A malicious source can preserve event handlers, unsafe links, or unescaped text that executes when the output file is opened.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds Block.html from raw node contents and concatenates those strings into final HTML. Scripts are removed earlier, but attributes and unescaped text are not sanitized.

content.value_statement: Teams often need quick presentations from articles, reports, and notes. OpenShow converts common document formats and URLs into a single playable HTML slideshow.
actual_capabilities: Converts Markdown, DOCX, PDF, TXT, local HTML, and URLs into HTML slides.
Extracts main page content from HTML or web pages with BeautifulSoup.
Inlines CSS, JavaScript, and images into one portable HTML file.
Builds cover, text, list, split, image, and closing slide layouts.
Adds keyboard, touch, fullscreen, progress, and timer controls.
Can open the generated deck in a browser when flags are used.
limitations: It does not support PPTX or legacy DOC input.
Remote URL and image conversion requires network access.
Complex web pages may not extract the exact article body.
Large PDFs or image-heavy documents can create large HTML files.

use_cases.title: Prepare Meeting Briefings
use_cases.description: Convert Markdown notes or a DOCX report into slides for fast internal review.

use_cases.title: Teach From Source Material
use_cases.description: Turn PDF handouts, text outlines, or web articles into a classroom deck.

use_cases.title: Share Technical Summaries
use_cases.description: Create a portable HTML deck from project documentation or release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion from one local file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use open-show to convert notes.md into a playable HTML slideshow in ~/openshow_outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a structured document into presentation slides.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use open-show to convert the DOCX project report into an HTML deck and tell me the output path.

prompt_templates.title: Build From a Web Article
prompt_templates.scenario: Create slides from a trusted URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use open-show to convert this article URL into a single-file HTML presentation, then summarize any extraction limits.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Open a Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use open-show to convert this PDF, save it to ~/openshow_outputs, and open the generated deck only after confirming with me.

output_examples.input: A Markdown planning note is converted into a deck.
output_examples.output: A single HTML file is created with section-based slides, navigation controls, and a timer.

output_examples.input: A trusted web article is converted for a team briefing.
output_examples.output: The main article content becomes a slide deck with images inlined when downloads succeed.

output_examples.input: A PDF handout is converted for classroom display.
output_examples.output: Each PDF page is embedded as an image slide in one playable HTML file.

best_practices: Review the generated slides before presenting them.
Use trusted URLs and documents, especially when opening generated HTML.
Keep source files small for reliable conversion and portable output.
anti_patterns: Do not use sensitive or untrusted documents without reviewing the output.
Do not expect pixel-perfect extraction from complex web pages.
Do not use it as a PPTX editor or full design suite.

faq.question: What formats does OpenShow support?
faq.answer: It supports Markdown, DOCX, PDF, TXT, local HTML, and HTTP or HTTPS URLs.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Local files do not require internet access. URL conversion and remote image inlining require network access.

faq.question: Can it create PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: No. It creates a playable HTML slideshow, not a PPTX file.

faq.question: Where are slides saved?
faq.answer: The command writes the generated HTML file to the output directory supplied by the user.

faq.question: Does it work on mobile?
faq.answer: Yes. The generated deck includes responsive layout and touch navigation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
